items.html: Angiotensin-converting enzyme in sarcoidosis. Angiotensin-converting enzyme levels are elevated in 40 to 80% of patients with sarcoidosis. Other laboratory findings include leukopenia, eosinophilia, an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, hypercalcemia in about 5% of patients and hypercalciuria.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 25, 44

src.question: Which laboratory result is elevated in 40 to 80% of patients with sarcoidosis?
src.explanation: Angiotensin-converting enzyme levels are elevated in 40 to 80% of patients with sarcoidosis. Other laboratory findings include leukopenia, eosinophilia, an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, hypercalcemia in about 5% of patients and hypercalciuria.

items.html: Methotrexate. Methotrexate is one of the immunosuppressants most commonly used when sarcoidosis is corticosteroid-intolerant or refractory, and it treats many autoimmune diseases such as lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. It is also implicated as a cause of interstitial lung disease.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 9, 12, 18, 46, 72

src.question: Which drug is both an immunosuppressant used in sarcoidosis and a listed cause of interstitial lung disease?
src.explanation: Methotrexate is one of the immunosuppressants most commonly used when sarcoidosis is corticosteroid-intolerant or refractory, and it treats many autoimmune diseases such as lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. It is also implicated as a cause of interstitial lung disease in the drug list and the treatment-related box.

items.html: Episodic presentation. An episodic presentation is less common in interstitial lung disease and can be seen with hypersensitivity pneumonitis, where inhaled organic material leads to illness after exposure; symptoms can be reversible if the problem is caught early.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 22, 65

src.question: Which interstitial lung disease can produce an episodic presentation?
src.explanation: An episodic presentation is less common in interstitial lung disease and can be seen with hypersensitivity pneumonitis, where inhaled organic material leads to illness after exposure, and symptoms can be reversible if the problem is caught early.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Laboratory tests, imaging and pulmonary function
items.html: Reticular opacities on the chest film. Among reticular opacities, fine ground-glass change is an early finding and medium reticular change, honeycombing, is a late finding. Moving from ground glass to honeycombing marks progression, consistent with fibrosis, which damages the alveoli permanently.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 5, 26

src.question: A 61-year-old woman with interstitial lung disease had a chest film 5 years ago showing fine reticular, ground-glass opacities. Her new film shows medium reticular opacities described as honeycombing. How should this change be classified?
src.key: Progression from early to late disease
src.explanation: Among reticular opacities, fine ground-glass change is an early finding and medium reticular change, honeycombing, is a late finding. Moving from ground glass to honeycombing over 5 years marks progression, consistent with fibrosis, which damages the alveoli permanently.

items.html: Onset patterns. Interstitial lung disease can present acutely over days to weeks, subacutely over weeks to months, chronically over months to years, or episodically. The episodic pattern of recurrent bouts is less common and can be seen with hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slide 22

src.question: A 44-year-old man has had four separate bouts of cough and dyspnea over the past year, each clearing completely between bouts. Which onset pattern of interstitial lung disease does his course fit?
src.explanation: Interstitial lung disease can present acutely over days to weeks, subacutely over weeks to months, chronically over months to years, or episodically. The episodic pattern of recurrent bouts is less common and can be seen with hypersensitivity pneumonitis, which makes his exposures worth reviewing.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Interstitial lung disease: what it is and what causes it
items.html: Drug-induced interstitial lung disease. Nitrofurantoin is one of the treatment-related causes of interstitial lung disease, beside radiation, methotrexate, amiodarone and chemotherapeutics, and it is also named among drugs that cause pulmonary toxicity. Exertional dyspnea, dry cough, crackles and restriction after years of use fit a drug cause.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 12, 23, 24, 35, 40, 72

src.question: A 66-year-old woman has taken nitrofurantoin for years to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections. Over several months she has developed progressive exertional dyspnea and a dry cough, with bibasilar inspiratory crackles and a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing. She has no occupational, bird or mold exposures. What is the most likely cause of her interstitial lung disease?
src.explanation: Nitrofurantoin is one of the treatment-related causes of interstitial lung disease, beside radiation, methotrexate, amiodarone and chemotherapeutics, and it is also named among drugs that cause pulmonary toxicity. Years of use followed by exertional dyspnea, dry cough, crackles and restriction fit a drug cause.

items.section_title: 3.1 · Interstitial lung disease: what it is and what causes it
items.html: Occupational and environmental exposures. Exposures are grouped as inorganic dusts, organic dusts and fumes or gases. Stone work releases free crystalline silica, and pneumoconiosis is caused by inhaled coal dust or various inorganic or silicate dusts, so stone work is an inorganic dust exposure.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 12, 13, 50, 60, 65

src.question: A 52-year-old man has spent 20 years cutting and polishing stone in a quarry. He now has progressive exertional dyspnea and a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing. How is his occupational exposure classified?
src.explanation: Occupational and environmental exposures are grouped as inorganic dusts, organic dusts and fumes or gases. Stone work releases free crystalline silica, and pneumoconiosis is caused by inhaled coal dust or various inorganic or silicate dusts, so his exposure is an inorganic dust.

items.html: Lupus pernio. Lupus pernio, skin sores on the face, is the skin involvement of sarcoidosis. A dry cough, insidious dyspnea, nontender lymphadenopathy and liver and spleen enlargement complete its multi-organ picture. Sarcoidosis also occurs more often in Black patients and in women.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 18, 25, 35, 39, 40, 42, 43

src.question: A 38-year-old Black woman has a dry cough and dyspnea of insidious onset. She has lupus pernio (skin sores on the face), nontender lymphadenopathy and liver and spleen enlargement. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.explanation: Lupus pernio, skin sores on the face, is the skin involvement of sarcoidosis, and a dry cough, insidious dyspnea, nontender lymphadenopathy and liver and spleen enlargement complete its multi-organ picture. Sarcoidosis also occurs more often in Black patients and in women.

items.html: Advanced disease. Right heart failure appears with advanced interstitial lung disease, and dyspnea that has spread from exertion to rest also marks progression. Early in the disease the examination may be normal.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 22, 23, 24, 73

src.question: A 76-year-old man has had interstitial lung disease for 9 years, and his dyspnea now occurs at rest. An echocardiogram shows right heart failure. What does the right heart failure indicate about his lung disease?
src.key: It is at an advanced stage
src.explanation: Right heart failure appears with advanced interstitial lung disease, and dyspnea that has spread from exertion to rest also marks progression. Early in the disease the examination may be normal, so these findings place him late in a long, chronic course.

items.html: Silicosis presentation. Sandblasting is a free crystalline silica exposure, and silicosis shows silicotic nodules 1-10 mm across throughout the lungs with eggshell calcification of the periphery of the hilar lymph nodes. Dyspnea, cough, weight loss, fatigue and crackles fit its presentation.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 26, 44, 58, 60, 61, 63, 69

src.question: A 48-year-old man has worked as a sandblaster for 20 years. He has dyspnea, cough, weight loss and fatigue with crackles on examination. His chest film shows nodular opacities, 1-10 mm across, throughout both lungs, and eggshell calcification of the periphery of the hilar lymph nodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.explanation: Sandblasting is a free crystalline silica exposure, and silicosis shows silicotic nodules 1-10 mm across throughout the lungs with eggshell calcification of the periphery of the hilar lymph nodes. Dyspnea, cough, weight loss, fatigue and crackles fit its presentation.

items.html: Methotrexate to avoid. Methotrexate is one of the immunosuppressants used for corticosteroid-refractory sarcoidosis, but it has also been implicated as a cause of interstitial lung disease. Azathioprine or infliximab covers the same refractory indication, so methotrexate should be avoided in a patient whose lung injury it already implicated.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 12, 18, 46, 47

src.question: A 47-year-old man with cardiac sarcoidosis has corticosteroid-refractory disease. He also has rheumatoid arthritis, and methotrexate he once took for it was stopped after it was implicated in lung injury. His team is weighing methotrexate, azathioprine, infliximab and continued corticosteroids. Which of these should be avoided?
src.explanation: Methotrexate is one of the immunosuppressants used for corticosteroid-refractory sarcoidosis, but it has also been implicated as a cause of interstitial lung disease, and in him it already was. Azathioprine or infliximab covers the same refractory indication without that history.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Laboratory tests, imaging and pulmonary function
items.html: Restrictive pattern on testing. Interstitial lung disease stiffens the lung so it no longer expands, giving a restrictive pattern: total lung capacity and forced vital capacity fall while the ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity stays normal or rises.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 4, 23, 24, 26, 29

src.question: A 58-year-old woman has 8 months of progressive exertional dyspnea and a persistent nonproductive cough, with bibasilar dry rales and small lung volumes on examination. Which combination of total lung capacity and ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity is expected?
src.key: Low capacity, normal or high ratio
src.explanation: Interstitial lung disease stiffens the lung so it no longer expands, giving a restrictive pattern: total lung capacity and forced vital capacity fall while the ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity stays normal or rises. Her small lung volumes on examination fit.

items.html: Complications of silicosis. The complications of silicosis are an increased risk of tuberculosis, progressive massive fibrosis and scleroderma. Scleroderma is also one of the connective tissue diseases that produce interstitial lung disease.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 18, 25, 64

src.question: A 50-year-old woman who has cut and polished stone for 22 years has silicosis. Her clinician reviews the known complications of silicosis, one of which is a connective tissue disease. Which connective tissue disease is it?
src.explanation: The complications of silicosis are an increased risk of tuberculosis, progressive massive fibrosis and scleroderma. Scleroderma is also one of the connective tissue diseases that produce interstitial lung disease, so new findings in her deserve that thought.

items.section_title: 3.3 · Laboratory tests, imaging and pulmonary function
items.html: Restrictive pattern. A restrictive pattern is a normal or increased ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity (normal 0.70 or more) with decreased total lung capacity and forced vital capacity (normal 80% or more of predicted).
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 26, 29, 34

src.question: A 63-year-old woman with exertional dyspnea and bibasilar crackles has pulmonary function testing: forced vital capacity 58% of predicted (normal 80% or more), total lung capacity 61% of predicted (normal 80% or more), and a ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity of 0.86 (normal 0.70 or more). How is this pattern classified?
src.explanation: A restrictive pattern is a normal or increased ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity with decreased total lung capacity and forced vital capacity. Her ratio of 0.86 is preserved while both capacities sit near 60% of predicted, the pattern interstitial lung disease produces.

items.html: Recovery after acute respiratory distress syndrome. Long-term recovery includes treating physical sequelae: post-intensive care muscle wasting, weakness and persistent fatigue. Rehabilitation addresses them while lung function continues to improve over 6 to 12 months.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 48, 54, 71, 74

src.question: A 66-year-old man is recovering after 3 weeks in the intensive care unit for acute respiratory distress syndrome. He has muscle wasting, weakness and persistent fatigue. Which referral addresses these problems?
src.explanation: Long-term recovery after acute respiratory distress syndrome includes treating physical sequelae: post-intensive care muscle wasting, weakness and persistent fatigue. Rehabilitation addresses them while his lung function continues to improve over 6 to 12 months.

items.html: Corticosteroids in sarcoidosis. Hypercalcemia (calcium above the 8.5-10.5 mg/dL range) is one of the indications for oral corticosteroids in sarcoidosis. About 90% of cases respond to corticosteroids, so they come first even when the chest film shows hilar adenopathy alone.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 44, 46, 47, 48, 71

src.question: A 38-year-old woman with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis has bilateral hilar adenopathy alone on chest film and no eye, heart or nervous system involvement. Her serum calcium is 11.9 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5). Which treatment is indicated?
src.explanation: Her calcium of 11.9 mg/dL is above the 8.5-10.5 range, and hypercalcemia is one of the indications for oral corticosteroids in sarcoidosis. About 90% of cases respond to corticosteroids, so they come first even when the chest film shows hilar adenopathy alone.

items.html: Management of coal workers' pneumoconiosis. Management is supportive, with oxygen, vaccinations, rehabilitation and smoking cessation, and in severe cases lung transplant may be indicated.
cites: Inflammatory Lung Disease 2026.pptx, Slides 48, 54, 74

src.question: A 56-year-old coal miner has severe complicated coal workers' pneumoconiosis with worsening dyspnea despite oxygen, vaccinations, pulmonary rehabilitation and smoking cessation. Which referral may be indicated?
src.explanation: Management of coal workers' pneumoconiosis is supportive, with oxygen, vaccinations, rehabilitation and smoking cessation, and in severe cases lung transplant may be indicated. He has severe disease that is worsening despite every supportive measure on the list.

items.section_title: 1.7 · The four waveforms of a normal EEG
items.html: What shapes the electroencephalogram. The intensity and patterns of electrical activity on the electroencephalogram are determined by the level of excitation of different parts of the brain, which varies with sleep, wakefulness and brain disorders such as epilepsy or psychosis.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 10, 21, 28

src.question: What determines the intensity and pattern of electrical activity on the electroencephalogram?
src.explanation: The intensity and patterns of electrical activity on the electroencephalogram are determined by the level of excitation of different parts of the brain, which varies with sleep, wakefulness and brain disorders such as epilepsy or psychosis.

items.section_title: 1.6 · The cycle between sleep and wakefulness
items.html: What ends wakefulness. After the brain has remained active for many hours, neurons in the activating system become fatigued. The positive feedback cycle between the mesencephalic reticular nuclei and the cerebral cortex fades, and the sleep-promoting centers take over.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 14, 18, 19

src.question: In the proposed theory, what ends a long period of wakefulness?
src.explanation: After the brain has remained active for many hours, neurons in the activating system become fatigued. The positive feedback cycle between the mesencephalic reticular nuclei and the cerebral cortex fades, and the sleep-promoting centers take over.

items.section_title: 1.5 · Why sleep matters: the physiological functions
items.html: Sleep restriction. Sleep restriction over a few days can decrease a person's cognitive and physical performance, overall productivity and health. That is one reason sleep is considered essential, even though its specific physiological functions are still being researched.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 9, 16, 17

src.question: Which outcome follows sleep restriction over a few days?
src.explanation: Sleep restriction over a few days can decrease a person's cognitive and physical performance, overall productivity and health. That is one reason sleep is considered essential, even though its specific physiological functions are still being researched.

items.html: Electrooculogram. The electrooculogram, the eye-movement recording, shows the irregular, sharply peaked eye movements of rapid eye movement sleep. The eye muscles are spared from the atonia that affects other voluntary muscles, so the eyes keep moving.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 10, 12, 28

src.question: Which recording shows the irregular, sharply peaked eye movements of rapid eye movement sleep?
src.explanation: The electrooculogram, the eye-movement recording, shows the irregular, sharply peaked eye movements of rapid eye movement sleep. The eye muscles are spared from the atonia that affects other voluntary muscles, so the eyes keep moving.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Slow-wave (non-rapid eye movement) sleep, and the comparison
items.html: Stage N3. Stage N3, also called deep sleep, is restful sleep and the deepest non-rapid eye movement stage, marked by delta waves. Body and tissue growth and repair occur in it, and it decreases with age.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 6, 9, 28

src.question: Which stage is the deepest sleep of the night?
src.explanation: Stage N3, also called deep sleep, is restful sleep and the deepest non-rapid eye movement stage, marked by delta waves. Body and tissue growth and repair occur in it, and it decreases with age.

items.html: Rapid eye movement episodes when sleepy. When a person is extremely sleepy, each rapid eye movement episode is short or even absent. As the person becomes more restful and less sleepy, the duration of rapid eye movement episodes increases, so the later periods of a night are longer.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 7, 9

src.question: Which circumstance makes rapid eye movement episodes short or even absent?
src.explanation: When a person is extremely sleepy, each rapid eye movement episode is short or even absent. As the person becomes more restful and less sleepy, the duration of rapid eye movement episodes increases, so the later periods of a night are longer.

items.html: Electromyogram. The electromyogram, the muscle recording, shows atonia of voluntary muscles in rapid eye movement sleep, sparing the eye muscles and diaphragm, as inactivity due to inhibited alpha motor neurons.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 12, 28

src.question: Which recording shows the atonia of voluntary muscles during rapid eye movement sleep?
src.explanation: The electromyogram, the muscle recording, shows atonia of voluntary muscles in rapid eye movement sleep, sparing the eye muscles and diaphragm, as inactivity due to inhibited alpha motor neurons.

items.section_title: 1.8 · EEG changes across wakefulness and sleep
items.html: Delta waves. Waves slower than 3.5 cycles per second with high voltage are delta waves, and delta waves mark stage N3, the deep, restful and deepest non-rapid eye movement stage, in which body and tissue growth and repair occur.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 25, 26, 27, 28

src.question: During sleep, the electroencephalogram shows high-voltage waves slower than 3.5 cycles per second. Which stage fits?
src.explanation: Waves slower than 3.5 cycles per second with high voltage are delta waves, and delta waves mark stage N3, the deep, restful and deepest non-rapid eye movement stage, in which body and tissue growth and repair occur.

items.html: Coma versus sleep. Arousability separates the two states: sleep is unconsciousness from which a person can be aroused by sensory or other stimuli, and coma is unconsciousness from which a person cannot be aroused. Failure to rouse to any stimulus points to coma.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 5, 10, 12, 14, 26, 28

src.question: In an unconscious person, which observation points to coma rather than sleep?
src.explanation: Arousability separates the two states: sleep is unconsciousness from which a person can be aroused by sensory or other stimuli, and coma is unconsciousness from which a person cannot be aroused. Failure to rouse to any stimulus points to coma.

items.html: Rapid eye movement sleep. Rapid eye movement sleep is the active, dreaming form of sleep: dreams are vivid, heart and breathing rates become irregular, and muscle tone is very depressed, with atonia of voluntary muscles except the eyes and diaphragm.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 9, 10, 14, 27, 28

src.question: Which state combines vivid dreaming, irregular heart and breathing rates, and very depressed muscle tone?
src.explanation: Rapid eye movement sleep is the active, dreaming form of sleep: dreams are vivid, heart and breathing rates become irregular, and muscle tone is very depressed, with atonia of voluntary muscles except the eyes and diaphragm.

items.section_title: 1.8 · EEG changes across wakefulness and sleep
items.html: Rapid eye movement sleep versus wakefulness. In rapid eye movement sleep the waves are irregular and high in frequency, beta waves like those of an awake, active person, which makes it often difficult to tell rapid eye movement sleep from alert wakefulness. Atonia of voluntary muscles is the difference.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 22, 25, 26, 28, 29

src.question: What shared electroencephalogram pattern makes rapid eye movement sleep hard to tell from alert wakefulness?
src.explanation: In rapid eye movement sleep the waves are irregular and high in frequency, beta waves like those of an awake, active person, which makes it often difficult to tell rapid eye movement sleep from alert wakefulness. Atonia of voluntary muscles is the difference.

items.section_title: 1.4 · Slow-wave (non-rapid eye movement) sleep, and the comparison
items.html: Non-rapid versus rapid eye movement physiology. Non-rapid eye movement sleep brings increased parasympathetic tone with low blood pressure, a slow heart rate and a decreased breathing rate, part of a 10 to 30% fall in vegetative functions. In rapid eye movement sleep, heart and breathing rates become irregular instead.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 10, 12, 14, 28

src.question: Which combination fits non-rapid eye movement sleep rather than rapid eye movement sleep?
src.key: Low blood pressure, slow heart rate
src.explanation: Non-rapid eye movement sleep brings increased parasympathetic tone with low blood pressure, a slow heart rate and a decreased breathing rate, part of a 10 to 30% fall in vegetative functions. In rapid eye movement sleep, heart and breathing rates become irregular instead.

items.html: Desynchronized sleep. Rapid eye movement sleep is also called desynchronized sleep because there is a lack of synchrony in neuron firing when there is brain activity. The tracing is irregular and high frequency, much like an awake, active person's.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 29, 22, 19

src.question: A 32-year-old woman's recording during a period of rapid eye movements shows irregular, high-frequency waves, and the technician labels it desynchronized sleep. What does that label describe?
src.explanation: Rapid eye movement sleep is also called desynchronized sleep because there is a lack of synchrony in neuron firing when there is brain activity. The tracing is irregular and high frequency, much like an awake, active person's, which fits her period of rapid eye movements.

items.html: Waking from rapid eye movement sleep. Rapid eye movement sleep is associated with vivid dreaming, and people can awaken spontaneously in the morning during rapid eye movement sleep; in a typical night the last rapid eye movement period leads into waking.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 9, 10, 13, 14, 7, 28

src.question: A 28-year-old woman wakes on her own at the end of a full night's sleep, recalling a vivid dream. From which sleep stage did she probably wake?
src.explanation: Rapid eye movement sleep is associated with vivid dreaming, and people can awaken spontaneously in the morning during rapid eye movement sleep; in a typical night the last rapid eye movement period leads into waking. Her spontaneous morning waking and vivid dream both point here.

items.html: Telling sleep from coma by arousal. Sleep is unconsciousness from which a person can be aroused by sensory or other stimuli; coma is unconsciousness from which a person cannot be aroused. Waking when shaken shows he was arousable, so he was asleep, even though a quieter stimulus had failed first.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 5

src.question: A 20-year-old college student is slumped over a library desk with his eyes closed. A friend says his name quietly and he does not respond, but when the friend shakes his arm he wakes and starts talking. Which finding shows he was asleep rather than in a coma?
src.key: He woke when his arm was shaken
src.explanation: Sleep is unconsciousness from which a person can be aroused by sensory or other stimuli; coma is unconsciousness from which a person cannot be aroused. Waking when his arm was shaken shows he was arousable, so he was asleep, even though a quieter stimulus had failed first.

items.html: Arousable unresponsiveness is sleep. A person who is unconscious yet is roused by a loud voice and a squeeze of the shoulder, and then answers questions, was asleep. Sleep is unconsciousness from which a person can be aroused by sensory or other stimuli.
cites: CMS 1 Phases of Sleep - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 5, 27, 28

src.question: A 68-year-old man on a medical ward is found late at night lying still with his eyes closed, not answering when the nurse enters the room. When she calls his name loudly and squeezes his shoulder, he opens his eyes and answers her questions. Which state best explains his earlier unresponsiveness?
src.explanation: He was unconscious, yet a loud voice and a squeeze of the shoulder roused him and he answered questions. Sleep is unconsciousness from which a person can be aroused by sensory or other stimuli, which is exactly what happened at his bedside.

items.section_title: 2.8 · The syllabus complications and comorbidities, one by one
items.html: Pulmonary hypertension in obstructive sleep apnea. Obstructive sleep apnea is classified with group 3 pulmonary hypertension, especially when it coexists with obesity hypoventilation syndrome or another cause of daytime hypoxemia. Right-sided heart failure from pulmonary hypertension is a late feature of obesity hypoventilation.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 11, 19, 20, 30

src.question: Pulmonary hypertension from obstructive sleep apnea is especially likely when the apnea coexists with which condition?
src.explanation: Obstructive sleep apnea is classified with group 3 pulmonary hypertension, especially when it coexists with obesity hypoventilation syndrome or another cause of daytime hypoxemia. Right-sided heart failure from pulmonary hypertension is a late feature of obesity hypoventilation.

items.section_title: 2.2 · Obstructive sleep apnea: who gets it and why
items.html: Enlarged tonsils. Enlarged tonsils are a risk factor and examination finding of obstructive sleep apnea, alongside obesity, macroglossia, micrognathia, retrognathia, a thick neck and a crowded posterior oropharynx. They point to structural narrowing of the upper airway.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 6, 7, 31

src.question: Which examination finding is a risk factor for obstructive sleep apnea rather than a screening feature for obesity hypoventilation syndrome?
src.explanation: Enlarged tonsils are a risk factor and examination finding of obstructive sleep apnea, alongside obesity, macroglossia, micrognathia, retrognathia, a thick neck and a crowded posterior oropharynx. They point to structural narrowing of the upper airway.

items.html: STOP-Bang worked total (4 and 3). Snoring 1 + observed apnea 1 + body mass index above 35 1 + neck 16 inches or larger 1 = 4; tiredness, pressure, age and gender (female) score 0. A total of 4 is intermediate, but yes to 2 of the first four questions plus a body mass index above 35 makes high risk. Snoring 1 + pressure 1 + age older than 50 1 = 3 is intermediate risk, and no combination rule applies.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: A woman answers yes to loud snoring and to being observed to stop breathing during sleep; her body mass index is 38 kg/m2 and her shirt collar is 16 inches. She is not tired during the day, is not treated for high blood pressure and is not older than 50. What is her STOP-Bang (snoring, tiredness, observed apnea, pressure, body mass index, age, neck, gender) total?
src.explanation: Snoring 1 + observed apnea 1 + body mass index above 35 1 + neck 16 inches or larger 1 = 4; tiredness, pressure, age and gender (female) score 0. A total of 4 is intermediate, but yes to 2 of the first four questions plus a body mass index above 35 makes her high risk.

also.explanation: Snoring 1 + pressure 1 + age older than 50 1 = 3; tiredness, observed apnea, body mass index (33 is not above 35), neck (15 is under 16 inches) and gender (female) score 0. A total of 3 is intermediate risk, and no combination rule applies.

items.html: Workup of obesity hypoventilation syndrome. Obesity hypoventilation syndrome is a diagnosis of exclusion: alternative causes of hypercapnia and hypoventilation must be excluded. The workup therefore includes a metabolic panel, blood count, thyroid function tests, pulmonary function tests, chest radiograph and toxicology screen.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 8, 32, 33

src.question: Why does the workup for obesity hypoventilation syndrome include a toxicology screen and thyroid function tests?
src.explanation: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome is a diagnosis of exclusion: alternative causes of hypercapnia and hypoventilation must be excluded. The workup therefore includes a metabolic panel, blood count, thyroid function tests, pulmonary function tests, chest radiograph and toxicology screen.

items.section_title: 2.6 · Obstructive sleep apnea: management, education and referral
items.html: Modafinil and armodafinil cautions. These stimulants need caution in patients with cardiovascular, hepatic or psychiatric conditions, so liver disease calls for care. They also have many potential drug interactions, and elderly patients receive lower doses.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 6, 8, 11, 12

src.question: In which patient are modafinil and armodafinil used with caution?
src.explanation: These stimulants need caution in patients with cardiovascular, hepatic or psychiatric conditions, so liver disease calls for care. They also have many potential drug interactions, and elderly patients receive lower doses.

items.html: Obesity criterion. Obesity for this diagnosis means a body mass index above 30 kg/m2, together with awake arterial carbon dioxide above 45 mmHg and exclusion of other causes. The syndrome becomes more likely as body mass index increases, and patients are typically obese and hypersomnolent.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 17, 28, 30, 32

src.question: What body mass index meets the obesity criterion for obesity hypoventilation syndrome?
src.explanation: Obesity for this diagnosis means a body mass index above 30, together with awake arterial carbon dioxide above 45 mmHg and exclusion of other causes. The syndrome becomes more likely as body mass index increases, and patients are typically obese and hypersomnolent.

items.html: High risk despite a total below 5. Snoring and tiredness are 2 of the first four questions, and a neck of 16 inches (40 cm) or larger completes a high-risk combination. The total is only 3, yet the person is high risk, as with 2 or more of the first four plus male gender or a body mass index above 35.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slide 17

src.question: On the STOP-Bang (snoring, tiredness, observed apnea, pressure, body mass index, age, neck, gender) questionnaire, which set of yes answers places a person at high risk despite a total below 5?
src.explanation: Snoring and tiredness are 2 of the first four questions, and a neck of 16 inches (40 cm) or larger completes a high-risk combination. The total is only 3, yet the person is high risk, as with 2 or more of the first four plus male gender or a body mass index above 35.

items.html: Obstructive sleep apnea history and examination. Loud habitual snoring, witnessed apneas, awakening with gasping, unrefreshing sleep, morning headaches, nocturia and poorly controlled hypertension are its history findings, and a large neck and a crowded posterior oropharynx are its examination findings. Narrowing of the upper airway by soft tissue or structure causes it.

src.question: A 48-year-old man has loud, habitual snoring, unrefreshing sleep, morning headaches and nocturia. His wife has seen him stop breathing and wake gasping. His blood pressure is poorly controlled on two medicines. His neck circumference is 18 inches, and his posterior oropharynx is crowded. What is the most likely diagnosis?
src.explanation: Loud habitual snoring, witnessed apneas, awakening with gasping, unrefreshing sleep, morning headaches, nocturia and poorly controlled hypertension are its history findings, and a large neck and a crowded posterior oropharynx are its examination findings. Narrowing of the upper airway by soft tissue or structure causes it.

items.html: Apnea and its obstructive type. An apnea is a 90% or greater fall in airflow on the thermistor lasting at least 10 seconds, and when airflow stops but respiratory effort continues, the apnea is obstructive. The airway collapses while the patient still tries to breathe.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 3, 24

src.question: A 52-year-old man's polysomnogram shows repeated events in which thermistor airflow falls by 90% or more for 15 seconds while chest and abdominal respiratory effort continue. How is each event classified?
src.explanation: An apnea is a 90% or greater fall in airflow on the thermistor lasting at least 10 seconds, and when airflow stops but respiratory effort continues, the apnea is obstructive. The airway collapses while the patient still tries to breathe, the event pattern of obstructive sleep apnea.

items.html: Modafinil and armodafinil side effects. Listed side effects include headaches, nervousness or anxiety, dizziness, nausea, and dermatologic and systemic hypersensitivities. A widespread rash with feeling unwell after starting the drug fits a dermatologic and systemic hypersensitivity reaction.

src.question: A 50-year-old man started modafinil for residual daytime sleepiness from obstructive sleep apnea. Two weeks later he develops a widespread rash and feels unwell. Which adverse effect of the drug best fits?
src.explanation: Listed side effects of modafinil and armodafinil include headaches, nervousness or anxiety, dizziness, nausea, and dermatologic and systemic hypersensitivities. A widespread rash with feeling unwell after starting the drug fits a dermatologic and systemic hypersensitivity reaction.

items.section_title: 2.4 · Obstructive sleep apnea: differential and diagnosis
items.html: Negative home sleep apnea test. At-home kits will not always diagnose mild obstructive sleep apnea; they are most helpful in moderate to severe disease. A negative home study with ongoing snoring and sleepiness therefore needs a polysomnogram, which can also find other sleep disorders a home kit cannot assess.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 8, 11

src.question: A 43-year-old woman with habitual snoring and daytime sleepiness has a home sleep apnea test that does not show obstructive sleep apnea. Her symptoms persist. What is the best next step?
src.explanation: At-home kits will not always diagnose mild obstructive sleep apnea; they are most helpful in moderate to severe disease. A negative home study in a woman with ongoing snoring and sleepiness therefore needs a polysomnogram, which can also find other sleep disorders a home kit cannot assess.

items.html: STOP-Bang risk bands. Snoring 1 + treated pressure 1 + age older than 50 1 + neck 17 inches 1 + male 1 = 5, the high-risk band (5 to 8); body mass index 35 does not count because it is not more than 35. Two yes answers to the first 4 questions plus male gender also make high risk. The low-risk band is 0 to 2: the body mass index rule needs 2 or more yes answers to the first 4 questions.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 16, 17

src.question: A 51-year-old man is evaluated before elective surgery. He snores loudly and is treated for high blood pressure. He feels rested during the day, and his wife has not seen him stop breathing. His body mass index is 35 kg/m2 and his neck (shirt collar) measures 17 inches. What is his STOP-Bang (snoring, tiredness, observed apnea, pressure, body mass index, age, neck, gender) score?
src.explanation: Snoring 1 + tired 0 + observed 0 + treated pressure 1 + body mass index 35 (not more than 35) 0 + age 51 (older than 50) 1 + neck 17 inches 1 + male 1 = 5, the high-risk band (5 to 8). He would also be high risk through 2 yes answers to the first 4 questions plus male gender.

also.explanation: Snoring 1 + tired 0 + observed 0 + pressure 0 + body mass index 36 (more than 35) 1 + age 35 0 + neck 14 inches 0 + female 0 = 2, the low-risk band (0 to 2). The body mass index rule needs 2 or more yes answers to the first 4 questions, and she has 1, so she stays low risk.

items.html: STOP-Bang worked example, score of 3. Snoring 1 + tired 1 + observed apnea 0 + pressure 0 + body mass index 38 (more than 35) 1 + age 50 (not older than 50) 0 + neck 15 inches 0 + female 0 = 3: intermediate by the count alone (3 to 4), but 2 yes answers to the first 4 questions plus a body mass index above 35 meet the questionnaire's added high-risk rule.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 16, 17

src.question: A 50-year-old woman reports loud snoring and feeling tired most days. No one has seen her stop breathing during sleep, and she is not treated for high blood pressure. Her body mass index is 38 kg/m2 and her neck (shirt collar) measures 15 inches. What is her STOP-Bang (snoring, tiredness, observed apnea, pressure, body mass index, age, neck, gender) score?
src.explanation: Snoring 1 + tired 1 + observed apnea 0 + pressure 0 + body mass index 38 (more than 35) 1 + age 50 (not older than 50) 0 + neck 15 inches 0 + female 0 = 3. The count alone is intermediate (3 to 4), and her 2 yes answers to the first 4 questions plus a body mass index above 35 meet the questionnaire's added high-risk rule.

items.html: Treating the elderly. Mortality from obstructive sleep apnea is lower in the elderly because they compensate, but they still have drowsiness and nocturia, and both improve with continuous positive airway pressure.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 22, 7

src.question: A 79-year-old man with untreated obstructive sleep apnea has daytime drowsiness and nocturia. His daughter asks whether treatment is worthwhile at his age. What is accurate?
src.explanation: Mortality from obstructive sleep apnea is lower in the elderly because they compensate, but they still have drowsiness and nocturia, and both improve with continuous positive airway pressure. Treating him targets the symptoms that affect his daily life.

items.html: STOP-Bang worked example, score of 6. Snoring 1 + tired 0 + observed apnea 1 + treated pressure 1 + body mass index 33 (not more than 35) 0 + age 56 (older than 50) 1 + neck 16.5 inches (16 or larger) 1 + male 1 = 6; a score of 5 to 8 is the high-risk group for obstructive sleep apnea.
cites: CMS I Obstructive Sleep Apnea & Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome - Shah Fallsv.pptx, Slides 16, 17

src.question: A 56-year-old man is seen for evaluation before elective knee surgery and has no known sleep disorder. His wife says he snores loudly enough to be heard through closed doors and has seen him stop breathing during sleep. He denies daytime tiredness. He is treated for high blood pressure. His body mass index is 33 kg/m2 and his neck (shirt collar) measures 16.5 inches. What is his STOP-Bang (snoring, tiredness, observed apnea, pressure, body mass index, age, neck, gender) score?
src.explanation: Snoring 1 + tired 0 + observed apnea 1 + treated pressure 1 + body mass index 33 (not more than 35) 0 + age 56 (older than 50) 1 + neck 16.5 inches (16 or larger) 1 + male 1 = 6. A score of 5 to 8 places him in the high-risk group for obstructive sleep apnea before his surgery.
